item.title: 2026-08-11 Restaurants, Dress Codes, and Favorite Foods
item.description:
Session Overview

Participants swapped stories about working in and dining at restaurants, including tales of generous and demanding customers, unexpectedly high food prices, and being turned away for dress code violations. The group debated whether they qualified as ‘regulars’ anywhere and discussed favorite snacks and ice cream flavors from different cultures. The conversation wrapped up with a lively exchange about exercise habits and whether different activities really require different shoes.

item.title: 2026-08-08 Would You Travel Back in Time or Forward?
item.description:
Session Overview

The session opened with the idiom ’take the reins’ and its literal roots in horsemanship, before moving into a wide-ranging discussion on time travel — whether to revisit the past or leap into the future, and which moments participants would change or simply witness. Learners shared personal reflections on career choices, childhood memories, advances in medicine, and the value of living in the present. The hour ended with a lively round of the card game Apples to Apples, which brought in fresh vocabulary such as ‘frazzled,’ ‘pathetic,’ and ‘casual.’

item.title: 2026-08-06 Listening Apps, Accents, and Global Education Systems
item.description:
Session Overview

The session opened with a participant demonstrating a self-built browser-based dictation app that reads sentences aloud and scores how accurately listeners can transcribe them, leading to a discussion of pronunciation tools and speech-recognition services. Conversation then shifted to regional accents — including Southern American and British varieties — and the challenge of tonal languages such as Mandarin, Cantonese, and Vietnamese. The group wrapped up by comparing tutoring cultures, school discipline practices, and university pathways across several countries, sharing personal stories of childhood independence and long language-learning journeys.

item.title: 2026-08-01 AI Tools, Privacy, and the Art of Learning a Language
item.description:
Session Overview

The session centered on a custom transcription tool one participant built to record class conversations and turn them into vocabulary lists and study notes on a public website. The group discussed whether sharing personal conversations with cloud-based AI services raised privacy and confidentiality concerns, and how consent should work in that setting. The conversation then broadened into a rich exploration of how people best learn languages — weighing technology and speed against immersion, real-life relationships, and lived experience.

item.title: 2026-07-30 Shopping Habits, Southern Culture, and American History
item.description:
Session Overview

The class began with tips for visiting a large university campus, then shifted into American history through a discussion of LBJ’s presidency and the Voting Rights Act of the 1960s. Participants explored the concept of southern hospitality and how it contrasts with the busier pace of life in large northern cities, briefly touching on the novel ‘To Kill a Mockingbird’ as a cultural reference. The session closed with a lively comparison of online shopping platforms across several countries and a discussion of the advantages of visiting local farmer’s markets and independent shops in person.

item.title: 2026-07-28 Retirement Savings and Investment Strategies
item.description:
Session Overview

The class discussed how the US retirement system works, comparing social security, pensions, and 401(k) accounts. Learners also explored investment strategies including index funds, ETFs, and individual stocks, and discussed why most individual investors tend to underperform the broader market. The session ended with a conversation about compound interest, long-term holding strategies, and the emotional challenges of investing.

💬 Idioms

“bump up”

a sudden or noticeable increase in an amount or level

item.title: 2026-07-25 Business Talk: Startups, Big Companies, and Getting Down to Business
item.description:
Session Overview

Participants shared personal stories about entrepreneurship, job dreams, and career paths — from reselling furniture in a shipping container to dreaming of a coffee cart. The group debated the pros and cons of working for large versus small companies, and discussed whether children should gain early business experience. The session also touched on workplace dress codes and how office attire has grown more casual over time.

💬 Idioms

“get down to business”

to stop chatting or delaying and start focusing on the real task at hand

item.title: 2026-07-24 US Money, Payment Methods, and Number Conventions
item.description:
Session Overview

The class explored US coins and bills, focusing on how Americans write and say numbers — especially the difference between using a period as a decimal mark versus a comma as a thousands separator. Learners then compared payment habits in their home countries, discussing tap to pay, QR codes, Venmo, and even government-backed digital currencies. The session ended with a creative shop-building activity to practice writing prices and a round of the vocabulary card game Apples to Apples.

item.title: 2026-07-23 Austin Parks, Kayaking, and a Cross-Country Amtrak Adventure
item.description:
Session Overview

The class opened with a moral dilemma about choosing between two bad options, introducing the idiom ‘between a rock and a hard place.’ Learners then shared personal stories about driving as teenagers in Mexico, exploring Austin’s parks, and kayaking on Lake Travis, comparing outdoor culture and nighttime safety across South Korea, China, and the United States. One learner described a month-long solo Amtrak journey from San Diego through Chicago and back to Austin, sparking discussion about train passes, senior discounts, and spontaneous travel.

item.title: 2026-07-18 A Blessing in Disguise: Finding the Good in Bad Situations
item.description:
Today’s Idiom

a blessing in disguise

This lesson is built around the classic idiom ‘a blessing in disguise’ — used when something that first appears bad turns out to be beneficial in the end. Two closely related expressions and key vocabulary for talking about setbacks, recovery, and positive thinking round out the lesson. Corrections focus on the article and preposition errors that intermediate learners most commonly make with these phrases.

item.title: 2026-07-18 Nostalgia: Smells, Cars, and Places from the Past
item.description:
Session Overview

Participants shared weekly updates — from job searching and dementia research to a trip to San Diego and welding a backyard grill — before diving into the session’s main theme of nostalgia. Guided by the idiom of the week (‘cup of tea’), the group explored how smells, fermented foods, childhood sweets, and old cars can trigger vivid memories of the past. They also compared notes on revisiting once-beloved places like Guam, San Diego, and Austin, and discovering how much those places had changed.
